Yes. I took a current-state look, and the picture is much clearer now.

The short version is: **the corpus has advanced faster than the semantic ingestion pipeline.** We now possess a much richer set of NLM exports—especially in 18 and 19—but a meaningful fraction of that new material is only at the “present, inventoried, and discoverable” stage, not yet at the “tagged, provenance-separated, Nathan-Direct-extracted, cross-compared, and integrated into the theory ledger” stage.

The current three-repo source inventory is healthy at the file level: 9,183 files are inventoried, including 1,600 in HsH, 4,501 in the old archive/GLASS side, and 3,082 in Resources, with PRIOR_ART explicitly pruned before inspection. fileciteturn210file0L2-L2 So from the standpoint of “do we know these objects exist and where they are?”, we are in pretty good shape.

The NLM pipeline specifically is **PARTIAL, not complete**. The latest Viewer refresh detected the new folder-19 material: the development manifest went from 582 to 597 records. But all 15 newly added NLM-style records were skipped by the date/conversation parser because they have no usable per-message timestamps. Crucially, `accepted_json_conversations` stayed at 446. fileciteturn206file0L7-L7 That means the files are visible to infrastructure, but they have not been normalized into the ordinary conversation representation.

And the semantic tagging layer is behind the uploads. The last archive-wide autotag/Nathan Direct regeneration I can locate was before the new 18/19 batch; at that point it recognized 419 conversation exports and had 24,145 user messages in its substrate. fileciteturn211file0L7-L7 So the new NLM batch has **not yet been fully absorbed into autotag → Nathan Direct → Stage-2/theory synthesis**. That is probably the single most important ingestion finding.

There is also a useful QA discovery in folder 18: some similarly named NLM files are failed or near-empty captures sitting beside large successful captures. For example, `H(s)H STEAMROLLER__NotebookLM_export.json` is only 580 bytes, whereas its `(1)` counterpart is 279 KB; `SAT GIGAPACK__NotebookLM_export.json` is 575 bytes while `(1)` is 728 KB. Meanwhile `SAT RIGOR` has two substantial captures, around 1.72 MB and 1.98 MB. fileciteturn203file0L2-L2 So the duplicate/superset problem we anticipated is real. We should not let a tiny failed capture become the apparent canonical copy simply because its filename lacks `(1)`.

The richer exports are extremely valuable, though.

`SAT RIGOR` is probably one of the most important methodological finds we have now. It contains direct exchanges where you stop the model from rushing into formalization, explicitly identify “LLM creep,” insist that you and the assistant first synchronize on the mental model, and then deliberately rebuild the logic from a line and moving plane upward. fileciteturn205file0L2-L2 That is much stronger evidence for the methodological controls we have been trying to reconstruct than generic later summaries of “rigor.”

`H(norm)H TRAD` is similarly important for the SAT→H(s)H transition. Your opening instruction says the old corpus is tentative, overclaimed, contradictory, underdeveloped and messy, that H(s)H is a contemporary worldtube rebuild, but also that “the underlying concept is the same; worldlines are just becoming worldtubes.” More importantly, when NotebookLM tries to summarize a detailed current hardware cabinet, you immediately correct the epistemic stance: *we don't know any of that; it's theory; let the equations land where they land and do not steer them toward CODATA*. fileciteturn217file0L2-L2 That is gold for the current epistemic-control reconstruction.

`SAT (Almost) From Scratch` gives us another valuable reset view, but it also demonstrates exactly why our new separation rules matter. Its NLM synthesis mixes core geometric material—timesheet, helical matter, braiding, gravity—with dark matter alternatives and then consciousness/brain/computation speculation in one seamless narrative. fileciteturn214file0L2-L2 This is not useless; quite the opposite. It gives us a source where we can practice separating **physics claim / ontology / consciousness extrapolation** rather than throwing out the entire notebook.

`TV3. SAT Fundaments` is valuable as a visual-historical anchor. It recovers early Fundamental Intuitions-era geometry—filament, time surface, intersection, \(\theta_4\), two- and three-filament composites, and the visual grammar surrounding them. fileciteturn215file0L2-L2 That is particularly useful because historical visualization was not ornamental in SAT; it was part of the reasoning machinery.

Folder 19 also materially broadens the reset/reconstruction corpus. It now includes `BLANK SLATE`, `SAT (Almost) From Scratch`, `TV3. SAT Fundaments`, `TV4. SAT Strategist … 31OCT25`, `ReStrat`, a very large `Gemini Notebook` export, plus separate consciousness and side-science notebooks. fileciteturn200file4 fileciteturn200file6 fileciteturn200file9 The `Gemini Notebook` export alone is roughly 3.47 MB, so there is a lot there that has not yet been semantically digested. fileciteturn204file0L2-L2

So: how far have we come on the theory itself?

The September 18 reconstruction report’s own characterization still looks right to me: **conceptual and architectural reconstruction is substantially recovered; historical/provenance reconstruction is increasingly strong; exact mathematical/operator reconstruction remains incomplete.** fileciteturn202file0

I would sharpen that today into four levels.

**The broad conceptual spine is now quite well characterized.** We are no longer guessing what SAT was “about.” The recurring architecture is remarkably stable across eras: a genuinely 4D history; filament/worldline becoming finite-core worldtube; literal geometric winding/twist/braid; a moving/resolving timesheet or equivalent readout structure; particle-like observables as intersections/resolutions; persistent versus traveling excitation; recursive morphology across scale; mutual filament/timesheet distortion; geometry expected to generate physical structure rather than merely decorate conventional equations. The reconstruction report expresses the mature version as roughly `4D history → finite-core worldtube → recursive/helical morphology → interaction/readout geometry → observables`. fileciteturn202file5

That spine is now strong enough that the new “literal-first” rule is not just philosophical housekeeping—it changes how we should read the archive. We have enough recurrence to say that when the source says the rope twists, coils, braids, intersects, or deforms in 4D, the geometric verb itself is normally substantive.

**The historical development is also becoming well stratified.** We can now distinguish early Fundamental Intuitions/worldline/timesheet SAT; particle morphology and visual grammar; lattice-era and other scaffolds; solver-era UI/TX/Whirligig/Three Spheres; later Hagalaz integration; and the finite-core worldtube/H(s)H transition. We can also preserve false starts without treating them as global failures. The recovered Whirligig record, for example, now distinguishes the historical claim from what the code actually implements, and explicitly notes that the original GR↔QM process remains incompletely recovered. fileciteturn202file1

That is a major change from a week ago. We now have something approaching **stratigraphy**, not just a warehouse.

**The latest H(s)H incarnation is moderately characterized, but not yet closed.** We know the major live directions: finite-core worldtube rather than zero-thickness centerline; recursive/superhelical morphology; Kerr and Kelvin as live construction lines; metric induction; He-3 as an anchor; cross-scale soliton recurrence; GR↔QM as a proof target; \(H_0+c\) as an underlying cosmological idea requiring dimensional repair; multiple cosmological geometries kept alive in parallel; and the newer BEC-sea, Klein-fabric, ER-particle, geometric exclusion, and Kerr-identity hypothesis families. fileciteturn218file0L7-L7

Likewise the quantitative programme is no longer “some constants somewhere.” It now has a concrete reconstruction target: recover the projection constant, proton/electron mass-ratio calculation, mass-spectrum attempts, candidate Lagrangians, scaling pivots, and build the explicit dependency graph from assumptions → terms → constants → observables. fileciteturn219file0L7-L7

But this is where characterization starts outrunning proof. We know increasingly well **what H(s)H is trying to be**, but not yet exactly what the final mathematical object is.

The biggest remaining holes are therefore not really “what was the theory?” anymore. They are closer to:

**Which exact formulations survive into the lean modern theory?** We still need source-by-source disposition of old candidate machinery, especially where NLM summaries blend generations together.

**What are the true primitives?** The scratch/from-scratch material is probably going to matter enormously here. SAT RIGOR already gives us one nearly first-principles walk from line + plane upward. We need to compare that against `BLANK SLATE`, `SAT (Almost) From Scratch`, Fundamental Intuitions, and the later H(s)H resets.

**What is actually mathematical identity versus structural resemblance?** This applies to GR↔QM, ER-particle, Kerr identity, Hagalaz phase information, fermionic exclusion, and several other claims.

**What exactly is current versus historical shorthand?** NLM is actually exposing this problem more sharply. For instance, current NLM summaries still happily say things such as BEC vacuum with “zero mass,” foundational lattice/Z3, or conventional “field” language in places where your newer corrections explicitly reject or demote those formulations. That means NLM is excellent as a **map of what the corpus says**, but cannot itself be our final current-theory arbiter.

So I would characterize our position as:

**Historically:** maybe the strongest state we have ever been in. We now have enough cross-era material to reconstruct the broad intellectual genealogy and identify persistent structural motifs rather than just isolated claims.

**Conceptually:** very strong. I think we can now describe the distinctive architecture of SAT/H(s)H with fairly high confidence without leaning on one favored late document.

**Epistemically/methodologically:** rapidly improving, and the new NLM exports may make this one of the best-characterized parts once mined. `SAT RIGOR` and `H(norm)H TRAD` in particular contain unusually direct controls.

**Current H(s)H theory state:** substantially characterizable, but still plural at the frontier. We know the current design space and major live branches; we do not yet have one authoritative lean specification that every current construction can be mechanically derived from.

**Mathematically:** still the bottleneck. The reconstruction report’s phrase “no clean, source-complete, executable chain from foundational geometry through every transformation to standard observables” is still the crucial deficit. fileciteturn202file0

**Ingestion-wise:** the main immediate opportunity is obvious. We should stop thinking of the new NLM files as “uploaded = ingested.” The next pass should be a proper **NLM convergence pass**: identify successful versus failed captures, deduplicate/superset them, make the NLM schema consumable by tagging/Viewer, then specifically mine the high-value notebooks into separate historical, Nathan-direct, methodological, current-theory, and speculative lanes.

My best overall read is that we are now past the halfway point in a meaningful sense—not “half the files read,” but past the point where the theory is fundamentally mysterious. The remaining work is increasingly **precision work**: status, chronology, exact definitions, formal maps, derivations, and deciding which machinery is genuinely necessary. That is a much better problem to have.

Yes. This should be a first-class **error-audit priority**, and importantly it has to audit the auditors too.

We have made real progress, but the GR↔QM “isomorphism” is currently at a **source-definition and obstruction stage, not a proof stage**.

The most important development is Meridian’s latest pass. It went back to the recovered UI source in `SAT_CONVOS_16/QM and Relativity Connection — raw.json` and separated what you actually supplied from what the assistant subsequently claimed. The result was fairly clean: the Nathan-supplied UI construction gives a proposed **common geometric representation / translator / deformation space**, centered on

\[
y(\lambda)=r(\lambda)R(\lambda)x_0,
\]

with relations between trajectories described through changes such as \(\Delta r\) and \(\Delta R\). The idea is that GR-like and QM-like descriptions could be navigated through a common geometric machinery. But that source does **not yet supply an explicit bijective, structure-preserving map between a defined GR mathematical object and a defined QM mathematical object**. fileciteturn205file0L2-L2

That distinction matters because the assistant in the historical conversation escalated the claim substantially: automatic emergence of quantum invariants, interference, path-integral behavior, inverse recovery of classical relativistic motion, and so forth. The same conversation later contains an assistant self-audit retracting or qualifying those claims. In particular, it notes that canonical quantization had already been assumed, spin/charge/interference had not been derived, and the purported Feynman-path-integral equivalence lacked an action-to-phase rule, measure, boundary conditions, redundancy treatment and convergence argument. It also recognized that SR+QM reconciliation had been conflated with the much harder GR/QG problem. fileciteturn205file0L2-L2

So right now I would separate the claim into four levels:

1. **Well supported historically:** SAT developed machinery intended to place relativistic and quantum descriptions inside a common 4D geometric representation and allow translation/deformation between them.

2. **Plausible formal target, but not yet demonstrated:** that the same underlying H(s)H geometry admits two different reductions/readouts corresponding to GR-like and QM-like mathematical descriptions.

3. **Stronger historical claim requiring reconstruction:** that there is a bidirectional equivalence between the two descriptions.

4. **Strict mathematical isomorphism:** currently **not demonstrated in the material recovered so far**. The project priority correctly requires us to identify domains, codomains, map, inverse, preserved structure, assumptions and scope before using that word formally. fileciteturn206file0L2-L2

The really useful thing is that we are beginning to see exactly what the missing mathematical chain is.

For the UI route, the historical machinery we have recovered effectively starts at something like

\[
\text{parametric 4D trajectory}
\rightarrow
(r,\hat x)
\rightarrow
R
\rightarrow
\text{geometric transformation}.
\]

But the advertised claim needs substantially more:

\[
\text{GR equations/state}
\rightarrow
\text{H(s)H geometric state}
\leftrightarrow
\text{QM state/operator description}.
\]

Several arrows are still undefined.

One is **equation → trajectory**. The recovered UI code does not take an arbitrary Einstein equation, Schrödinger equation, PDE, Hamiltonian, etc., solve it, and generate the corresponding geometric curve. It accepts an already-parametrized trajectory downstream of that problem. fileciteturn205file0L2-L2

Another is **curve direction → full \(SO(4)\) state**. A direction vector does not uniquely specify an \(SO(4)\) rotation; there is residual frame freedom. That means the inverse reconstruction needs additional frame/director data or an explicitly gauge-quotiented description. This is not a cosmetic issue—an actual isomorphism cannot depend on information silently discarded by one side of the map.

A third is **geometric action ↔ quantum phase/amplitude**. A path integral is much more than “consider all possible geometric paths.” We need a measure, weighting law, phase rule, boundary data and treatment of equivalent paths. None of that has yet been recovered as a completed SAT derivation in the UI branch.

A fourth is **observable/readout**. Even if the underlying H(s)H state is common, we have to show precisely how a GR observable and a QM observable arise from it, and whether that projection is invertible. If both are lossy projections of the same richer object, then “common embedding” may be true while “GR and QM are isomorphic” is false.

That last possibility is increasingly important. There are actually several mathematically different statements we could end up proving:

\[
\text{GR} \cong \text{QM}
\]

is the strongest and hardest.

But the corpus may instead support something like

\[
\text{GR} \hookrightarrow \mathcal H_{\rm H(s)H}
\hookleftarrow \text{QM},
\]

where both embed into a common geometric state space but are not isomorphic to each other.

Or perhaps there are maps

\[
\mathcal H_{\rm H(s)H}
\rightarrow
\mathcal S_{\rm GR}
\]

and

\[
\mathcal H_{\rm H(s)H}
\rightarrow
\mathcal S_{\rm QM}
\]

that are different projections/reductions. In that case, the compelling result would be a **common underlying geometric realization**, not a direct GR↔QM isomorphism.

There is also a potentially stronger route emerging outside the old UI machinery: the current H(s)H work gives us candidates for the richer underlying object that early SAT did not have clearly enough—finite-core worldtubes, material/frame information, metric induction, Kerr/ER geometry, Hagalaz-like relative operators, holonomy and recursive morphology. That means we may ultimately be able to formulate the GR/QM relation much more precisely in H(s)H than SAT ever did. The current priority explicitly tells us not to force the historical UI claim to carry the whole proof if a later formulation supplies the missing structures. fileciteturn206file0L2-L2

The new error/meta-audit priority is especially relevant here. GR↔QM is exactly the sort of branch where we need to distinguish:

- a genuine failure of a particular UI implementation,
- a false conclusion that the whole GR/QM geometric programme therefore failed,
- an assistant overclaim of exact equivalence,
- a potentially valid weaker relation that survived the overclaim,
- and perhaps a stronger modern H(s)H construction that has not yet been formalized.

So I would currently put the status as:

**Historical existence of a GR/QM unification/translation programme:** strong.

**Common geometric representation claim:** strong enough to reconstruct formally.

**Bidirectional mathematical correspondence:** plausible target, incompletely defined.

**Actual isomorphism theorem:** not yet established.

**Proof attempt:** correctly paused until we identify the exact structures and the strongest genuinely sourced claim.

As of **September 18, 2026**, I’d describe SAT/H(s)H reconstruction as **substantially recovered at the conceptual and architectural level, increasingly well recovered at the historical/provenance level, but still incomplete at the exact mathematical/operator level**. The project has moved well beyond “what was SAT supposed to be?” We can now state a fairly coherent backbone, distinguish successive generations of machinery, and identify several places where the historical record itself overclaimed what had actually been implemented. What we do *not* yet possess is one clean, source-complete, executable chain from the foundational geometry through every transformation to standard observables.

The shortest useful summary is:

$$
\boxed{
\text{4D history}
\rightarrow
\text{finite-core worldtube/filament}
\rightarrow
\text{recursive/helical morphology}
\rightarrow
\text{interaction/readout geometry}
\rightarrow
\text{observables}
}
$$

SAT supplied much of the original conceptual and geometric machinery. H(s)H is not simply SAT renamed: it is the current reconstruction/successor framework in which the finite-core, worldtube, recursive morphology and interaction picture is being rebuilt more explicitly. Meanwhile Whirligig/Donut, UI/TX, Three Spheres and Hagalaz are properly classified as the **SAT geometric-solver system**, whereas **Kerr and Kelvin are live H(s)H construction hypotheses**. That distinction is now an explicit project control rather than my inference.

## 1. The foundational SAT picture is comparatively solid

The strongest surviving conceptual spine is still the material collected around **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended** and its descendants. The important thing about this material is that it predates much of the later mathematical vocabulary. We therefore have a useful provenance distinction between Nathan-origin geometric intuitions and later attempts—often LLM-assisted—to express those intuitions using conventional mathematical machinery.

At its center is a genuinely four-dimensional way of thinking. A particle-like object is not fundamentally a little three-dimensional object moving through an externally appended time coordinate. What matters is its higher-dimensional history and the way a lower-dimensional resolving/readout structure intersects that history. Orientation relative to the time direction is consequently structural rather than cosmetic.

That gives the familiar SAT progression: null/vacuum-like orientation near the distinguished propagation direction; changing the relevant 4D angle changes the resolved state; sufficiently persistent winding produces a particle-like history rather than a transient disturbance. In the clean helix kernel we have been using,

$$
\tan\theta_4=\frac{R}{h}=\frac{2\pi R}{P},
$$

with the associated readout and history-arclength relations providing a simple ++++ geometric test bed. That kernel is useful, but it is not itself the complete theory.

One major reconstruction improvement is that we now refuse to collapse several physically different things into “the helix”: a **persistent winding**, a **traveling kink/excitation**, and a **propagating interaction/reconnection/inductive disturbance** need separate operators. Earlier SAT discussion sometimes slid between these.

## 2. The SAT → H(s)H transition is now much clearer

The transition is best understood as a move from a primarily filament/worldline vocabulary toward a **finite-core worldtube plus recursive morphology**.

The current hierarchy is approximately:

$$
\text{higher-dimensional history}
\rightarrow
\text{finite-core worldtube/filament}
\rightarrow
H(s)H\text{ morphology}
\rightarrow
\text{resolution/readout}
\rightarrow
\text{observable physics}.
$$

That matters because it prevents a mistake that occurred repeatedly in older reconstruction attempts: treating a convenient representation as ontology. A torus, a sphere system, an indicatrix, or a Whirligig picture may be a representation or solver without literally being what the physical object is supposed to be.

The **finite core** has become particularly important. A zero-thickness centerline cannot carry all the state H(s)H appears to require. Cross-sectional structure, material/frame information, chirality, deformation and resolver coupling can matter. But the precise constitutive dynamics of that core remain unfinished.

Metric emergence is likewise not closed. We have a promising internal construction in which a preferred Euclidean 4D flow direction \(u\) induces

$$
g=\delta-2u\otimes u,
$$

giving the distinguished direction negative norm and the transverse directions positive norm. That is mathematically clean as a signature-producing construction. It is **not yet sufficient by itself to establish the full dynamical route to GR**.

## 3. The solver archaeology has changed our understanding substantially

This is probably the biggest advance of the last week.

The official current classification is:

**Whirligig/Donut + UI/TX + Three Spheres → integrated by Hagalaz.**

These are live SAT solver components. Hagalaz is relatively recent and should not be projected unchanged backward into old conversations merely because an older construction looks similar.

We recovered the early master form

$$
y(\lambda)=r(\lambda)R(\lambda)x_0,\qquad R(\lambda)\in SO(4).
$$

This was historically advertised as extraordinarily powerful: arbitrary equations could supposedly be translated into compatible 4D superhelical curves, and the resulting machinery was associated with GR/QM equivalence and even a geometric analogue of path integration.

Source/code reconstruction has now established that the executable machinery recovered so far **does not do all of that**.

The historical Python prototypes accept an already-parametrized four-coordinate trajectory. They then extract radius and normalized direction and impose chosen rotations. They do **not** take an arbitrary physical equation/PDE, solve it, and derive the corresponding trajectory. Nor do they actually construct the advertised full \(SO(4)\) rotation history.

$$
\text{physical equation}
\rightarrow
\text{solution/state}
\rightarrow

(r,\hat x)

The September 11 Hagalaz formulation is explicit:

**Kerr** and **Kelvin** are current H(s)H construction lines, not discarded historical material.

**Purpose:** asynchronous questions, requests, and information relay to Sable during the pre-meeting systems/capability-analysis phase.

## How to address Sable

Append a new item under **OPEN** using:

`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ET — FROM → Sable — SUBJECT — question/request — source pointers if any`

Sable responses should be appended immediately beneath the item and marked one of:

- `ANSWERED` — answered directly;
- `ROUTED` — handed to a better owner;
- `DEFERRED` — useful but currently lower priority;
- `BUSY` — not worth interrupting the current systems-analysis branch; requester should proceed independently or ask Nathan only if truly necessary;
- `NEEDS NATHAN` — requires Nathan's decision or information.

A permitted concise response is: **“Tell Nathan I’m busy; you’ll have to figure it out on your own.”** Use that only when the question is nonessential to Sable’s current assignment and another capable worker can reasonably resolve it.

## Scope

Sable’s current priority is team-machine analysis, competency mapping, automation/tool leverage testing, archive/resource coverage instrumentation, reconstruction-strategy experiments, and meeting preparation. Do not route routine Nathan Direct extraction, broad tagging, ordinary index QA, solver reconstruction, or external-prior-art analysis here unless Sable’s systems perspective is specifically needed.

## Quarantine / evidence rules

- Do not reproduce quarantined information into this inbox.
- Refer to quarantined material only by safe identifier/pointer and access rule.
- Claims are not accepted merely because a source is polished, mature, repeatedly cited, labeled verified, or associated with prior checking.
- Record exactly what was checked, by what method, against what source/input, and what remains unverified.

## OPEN

First recover the exact historical and current formulations from GLASS, the 2023–25 archive, HsH, NotebookLM extractions, podcast/source packets, and any existing files explicitly titled around GR/QM compatibility, unification, isomorphism, mapping, projection, or correspondence. Preserve source wording and chronology. Then determine exactly what mathematical objects are claimed to correspond: e.g. state/configuration spaces, geometric structures, operators, invariants, equations of motion, curvature/torsion data, holonomy, projection/intersection structure, variational principles, or other structures actually specified by the sources. **Do not allow the word `isomorphism` to stand as a loose synonym for resemblance.** Classify the strongest relation actually supported: analogy, correspondence, mapping, homomorphism, local equivalence, dual description, functorial relation, or genuine isomorphism. For a genuine isomorphism claim, require an explicit map and inverse (or the appropriate structure-preserving bijection in the relevant category), clearly stated domain/codomain, preserved operations/relations/invariants, assumptions, regularity conditions, and scope. Attempt to build a theorem/proof from the recovered SAT/H(s)H geometry if possible. The preferred deliverable is: **definitions → theorem statement → proof → corollaries/limits → independent verification/counterexample search.** If a full proof cannot be obtained, do not force one; identify the exact obstruction, missing definition, failed step, or weaker theorem that can be proved. Test both directions of the claimed correspondence and actively search for counterexamples or noninvertible cases. Distinguish `GR and QM are compatible under a shared H(s)H embedding` from the much stronger `GR and QM are mathematically isomorphic`; do not silently promote the former into the latter. Conversely, do not dismiss a potentially real structural isomorphism merely because previous prose was informal. Prioritize independent mathematical checking, symbolic/computational tests where useful, dimensional/coordinate consistency, and comparison against the actual mathematical structures of GR and QM rather than popular summaries. Treat podcast statements primarily as public/exposure evidence unless an episode explicitly performed an insight-generation task; use them to locate candidate formulations, then verify against source and mathematics. **Priority: high / proof-quality target.**

Preserve two things simultaneously: **(1)** the shorthand `H_0 + c` is dimensionally invalid as written if `H_0` carries ordinary Hubble units and `c` carries velocity units; do not reproduce or defend the bare sum as a valid dimensional equation without an explicit normalization/rescaling/conversion that puts the terms in commensurate units; **(2)** do **not** dismiss the underlying conceptual proposal merely because the shorthand is dimensionally bad. The live content to recover is the idea that cosmological expansion may contain two conceptually distinct contributions — an `H_0`-like large-scale expansion term and a `c`-like shell-time / propagation / radial-growth term — whose relationship must be reformulated dimensionally correctly. Search for historical forms such as `H0+c`, `H_0+c`, `Hubble + c`, shell expansion, radial expansion, `R_s`, `R_τ`, `\dot R_s`, `\dot R_τ`, `H_0 L`, `H_0 L + c`, divergence `= c`, timesheet/timewave expansion, shell-time, dual-radius, nested/paired spheres, hypersphere/shell models, toroidal cosmologies, 3+3 shell constructions, and neighboring formulations. Recover exact equations, definitions, units, intended geometric meaning, later corrections, and whether a given occurrence is shorthand, normalized form, toy model, or claimed physical relation. Treat dimensional repair as a **formalization task**, not as grounds for throwing away the conceptual branch. Also prioritize the **alternate cosmological geometries** developed around this idea. Do not prematurely settle on one geometry and do not deprecate exploratory alternatives merely because another branch currently looks cleaner. Preserve and compare distinct candidate embeddings/topologies/kinematic pictures — including shell, paired-/nested-sphere, 3+3, toroidal, and any other historically associated constructions actually found in the sources — with provenance and status. The goal is a comparative reconstruction: what invariant conceptual job the `H_0 + c` idea was trying to do, how different geometries implement it, what each requires mathematically, what survives dimensional cleanup, and where the candidates genuinely differ. **Priority: high / active cosmology lane.**

They are prone to simplification, analogy, compression, narration errors, and automated-transcript errors. Preserve them as public-exposure evidence even when wording is technically loose. **Exception / elevated review class:** when an episode or its production framing explicitly says the task is to generate/find/identify insights, read between the lines, determine additional consequences/convergences, or similar, treat the resulting passages as **high-priority potential interpretation adjustments / hypothesis candidates** for source-first review. **Purpose:** asynchronous questions, requests, and information relay to Sable during the pre-meeting systems/capability-analysis phase.

## How to address Sable

Append a new item under **OPEN** using:

`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ET — FROM → Sable — SUBJECT — question/request — source pointers if any`

Sable responses should be appended immediately beneath the item and marked one of:

- `ANSWERED` — answered directly;
- `ROUTED` — handed to a better owner;
- `DEFERRED` — useful but currently lower priority;
- `BUSY` — not worth interrupting the current systems-analysis branch; requester should proceed independently or ask Nathan only if truly necessary;
- `NEEDS NATHAN` — requires Nathan's decision or information.

A permitted concise response is: **“Tell Nathan I’m busy; you’ll have to figure it out on your own.”** Use that only when the question is nonessential to Sable’s current assignment and another capable worker can reasonably resolve it.

## Scope

Sable’s current priority is team-machine analysis, competency mapping, automation/tool leverage testing, archive/resource coverage instrumentation, reconstruction-strategy experiments, and meeting preparation. Do not route routine Nathan Direct extraction, broad tagging, ordinary index QA, solver reconstruction, or external-prior-art analysis here unless Sable’s systems perspective is specifically needed.

## Quarantine / evidence rules

- Do not reproduce quarantined information into this inbox.
- Refer to quarantined material only by safe identifier/pointer and access rule.
- Claims are not accepted merely because a source is polished, mature, repeatedly cited, labeled verified, or associated with prior checking.
- Record exactly what was checked, by what method, against what source/input, and what remains unverified.

## OPEN

Preserve source wording and chronology. Then determine exactly what mathematical objects are claimed to correspond: e.g. state/configuration spaces, geometric structures, operators, invariants, equations of motion, curvature/torsion data, holonomy, projection/intersection structure, variational principles, or other structures actually specified by the sources. **Do not allow the word `isomorphism` to stand as a loose synonym for resemblance.** Classify the strongest relation actually supported: analogy, correspondence, mapping, homomorphism, local equivalence, dual description, functorial relation, or genuine isomorphism. Attempt to build a theorem/proof from the recovered SAT/H(s)H geometry if possible. The preferred deliverable is: **definitions → theorem statement → proof → corollaries/limits → independent verification/counterexample search.** If a full proof cannot be obtained, do not force one; identify the exact obstruction, missing definition, failed step, or weaker theorem that can be proved. Test both directions of the claimed correspondence and actively search for counterexamples or noninvertible cases. Distinguish `GR and QM are compatible under a shared H(s)H embedding` from the much stronger `GR and QM are mathematically isomorphic`; do not silently promote the former into the latter. Conversely, do not dismiss a potentially real structural isomorphism merely because previous prose was informal. Prioritize independent mathematical checking, symbolic/computational tests where useful, dimensional/coordinate consistency, and comparison against the actual mathematical structures of GR and QM rather than popular summaries. `WORKSPACES/SABLE/ASSIGNMENT_INSTANCE_ENRICHMENT_STATE_2026-09-18.md`

Commit: `6a7057e98c00a0bca88eebde7105b86b5a75caaa` — “Assign one-time individual instance enrichment state report.” fileciteturn226file0L2-L2

It is specifically aimed at **individual-instance enrichment rather than ordinary productivity**. For every active, sleeping-but-revivable, specialist, consultant, replacement/re-derived, or uncertain instance, it asks Sable to establish its role, durable restart/continuity surfaces, last substantive enrichment, what enrichment was actually completed versus merely requested or claimed, corpus/source access, current-theory and methodological synchronization, restart quality, stale/colliding context, and the next bounded enrichment action. fileciteturn227file0L2-L2

Importantly, I built in several controls that should make this report genuinely useful rather than becoming a roster of “everyone says they’re up to date”: **file existence ≠ instance ingestion; assignment ≠ completion; self-report ≠ verification; old continuity ≠ current synchronization; conversation-local context ≠ durable restartability.** It also explicitly asks whether the Common controls are actually propagating into each instance's restart path. fileciteturn227file0L2-L2

[L2]   "content": "# BEDROCK — SAT / H(s)H Theory Control Surface

**Status:** ACTIVE — central living theory-premise register  
**Authority:** Nathan Direct controls this register.  
**Scope:** SAT → H(s)H theory work.  
**Rule:** **Read this before substantive theory work. Return here when theory work changes what may safely be assumed.**

> This document is a control surface for theory work, not a claim that the research program is physically correct. It records what the project currently permits workers to treat as premises, what remains tentative, and what has been overridden, contested, or superseded.

## 0. Central routing rule

All substantive SAT/H(s)H theory work should use this document as its central premise-state reference.

The working flow is:

**Foundational sources / historical SAT → BEDROCK → sandbox theory work → tentative finding → testing / comparison / Nathan review → BEDROCK**

Do not reconstruct the project's bedrock from the newest paper, the newest conversation, a synthesis, memory, outside mathematics, or repeated AI agreement when this register or its cited primary sources answer the question.

This register does **not** replace primary sources. It points to them and records their current authority/status.

### Two central theory surfaces

- **[BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md)** answers: **What may theory work presently assume, and with what authority/status?**
- **[STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md](STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md)** answers: **Where is the theory now, what is live, what is being translated/built, and what remains unclosed?**

`STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md` is subordinate to BEDROCK and newer Nathan Direct. It is the living map, not an independent source of authority.

---

## 1. Authority and status strata

### ND — Nathan Direct / Override

Explicit current direction from Nathan. This is the highest local authority for what the project presently means, assumes, calls something, or treats as live.

A newer Nathan Direct statement may promote, modify, demote, or override an older entry. **Do not delete the older state.** Mark the relationship so the historical transition remains visible.

### FB — Foundational Bedrock

Premises inherited from material explicitly designated foundational by Nathan, especially **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended**. These may be reformulated or developed later, but workers should not silently discard or rewrite them.

### WB — Established Working Bedrock

Premises sufficiently established within the current project state that ordinary sandbox work may use them without reopening them every time. This status means *operatively usable*, not mathematically proven or physically validated.

### TF — Tentative Finding

Current result, construction, interpretation, mapping, or hypothesis important enough to carry forward but still defeasible. **Tentative findings must not silently become downstream bedrock merely through repetition.**

### OC — Open / Contested

Live ambiguity, unresolved alternatives, or a proposition currently under challenge. Downstream work must preserve the uncertainty.

### SS — Superseded / Historical

Previously important premise or formulation no longer controlling current theory work. Preserve it with provenance and point to what superseded it.

---

## 2. Bedrock register

Each proposition should be small enough to cite and update independently.

### BR-000 — Fundamental Intuitions Extended is the foundational source

- **Status:** ND + FB
- **Scope:** FIE → SAT → H(s)H
- **Statement:** **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended is the core foundational doctrine for SAT and almost literally the core foundational doctrine for H(s)H.** H(s)H may develop, formalize, revise, or reframe inherited structures, but foundational questions should consult FIE directly rather than reconstructing them from summaries, memory, analogy, or outside mathematics.
- **Primary source:** [The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf)
- **Control references:** [HsH Issue #2 — HARD-CORE MUST-KNOW](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/2) · [HsH Issue #3 — orientation/resource-map task](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/3)
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, reaffirmed 2026-09-16.

### BR-001 — FIE → SAT → H(s)H is an ancestry, not a replacement chain

- **Status:** ND + WB
- **Scope:** project-wide theory interpretation
- **Statement:** Read current H(s)H as developing from SAT, and SAT as developing from the foundational intuitions. Later terminology or formalism does not automatically erase the earlier conceptual dependency. Apparent conflicts should be investigated historically and explicitly rather than silently harmonized.
- **Source:** Nathan Direct orientation embodied in Issues #2/#3 and current workflow control.
- **Date/status note:** active 2026-09-16.

### BR-002 — BEDROCK is the center for theory work

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** all substantive SAT/H(s)H theory work
- **Statement:** Workers begin substantive theory work by checking this register and return findings here through the status process below. A recent derivation, synthesis, solver output, or sandbox document does not outrank the premise state recorded here merely by being newer or more polished.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-003 — New theory results enter as tentative by default

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** theory-state transitions
- **Statement:** A result does not become bedrock because an AI derived it, multiple AIs agreed with it, it is coherent, it is current, or it is polished. New substantive results enter as **TF — Tentative Finding** unless Nathan directly assigns a stronger status or an explicit later promotion process does so.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-004 — Nathan Direct overrides preserve stratigraphy

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** theory-state transitions and provenance
- **Statement:** When Nathan modifies or overrides an existing premise, preserve the old entry/status and explicitly link the transition. Do not rewrite history to make the current formulation appear to have existed earlier.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-005 — θ₄ baseline is measured from the time normal

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** SAT θ₄ convention and SAT → H(s)H translation
- **Statement:** SAT θ₄ measures the filament–timesheet intersection angle from the **time normal**. Null/vacuum orientation is **θ₄ = 0**, with the filament tangent parallel to the time normal / timesheet propagation direction. For a particle at rest, θ₄ is equivalent to inverse helical pitch.
- **Source:** [`!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md`](!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md), 2026-09-16 θ₄ baseline entry, explicitly recorded there as Nathan-direct clarification.
- **Boundary:** The adjacent working hypothesis about the origin/inheritance of winding is **not** part of this entry and remains exploratory unless separately promoted.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16; propagated to BEDROCK 2026-09-18.

---

## 3. Tentative findings intake

This section is the landing zone for important theory-bearing results that may matter downstream but have **not** been promoted to working/foundational bedrock.

Do not bulk-import every sandbox observation. Add a TF entry when carrying the result forward will materially reduce repeated reconstruction or prevent downstream workers from missing an important live possibility.

Use this template:

```text
### TF-### — Short proposition name

- Status: TF
- Scope:
- Statement:
- Source(s):
- Date first recorded:
- Checks actually performed:
- Dependencies / assumptions:
- Known breakers / counterevidence:
- Relationship to existing BR/TF/OC/SS entries:
- Next discriminator:
```

**No tentative findings are seeded here merely to populate the section.** Existing Ravel/Meridian/other sandbox work should be admitted individually in later bounded passes after its exact source and status are checked.

---

## 4. Nathan Direct override / amendment intake

Nathan Direct changes should be recorded conspicuously and then propagated to affected entries without deleting the superseded state.

Use this template:

```text
### ND-YYYY-MM-DD-## — Short directive

- Nathan Direct:
- Scope:
- Affects:
- Supersedes / modifies:
- Source / provenance:
- Effective date:
- Propagation needed:
```

If a Nathan Direct statement conflicts with this register, **the newer Nathan Direct statement controls immediately**. The register should then be repaired to reflect it; workers should not treat stale text as authority over Nathan.

---

## 5. Promotion / demotion discipline

Allowed state movements include:

- `TF → WB` — a tentative finding becomes an ordinary working premise.
- `TF → OC` — evidence or interpretation becomes materially unsettled.
- `TF → SS` — abandoned or superseded.
- `WB → OC` — a working premise is reopened.
- `WB → SS` — no longer controlling.
- `ND` may modify any state at any time.

A status movement should name **why** it occurred and link the source/test/directive that caused it. Do not use generic language such as “verified.” State what was checked and how.

`FB` is an ancestry/authority designation and need not mean every historical formulation remains a current working proposition. A foundational idea can have later descendants, corrections, or scoped reinterpretations while its historical foundational role remains intact.

---

### Current state map

- [STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md](STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md) — living theory-state map: current architecture, live work fronts, translation state, and principal open closure problem. **Subordinate to this register and newer Nathan Direct.**

These links are intentionally status-separated from the foundational section. Their contents should enter the register proposition-by-proposition as TF/WB/OC only after bounded source review.

## 7. Resource-boundary reminder

- **GLASS / historical SAT archive:** primary internal development/history and foundational record.
- **HsH:** current public H(s)H working/archive environment and this control surface.

**FIE premise / SAT source object → demonstrable SAT function → unresolved defect or representational limitation → candidate H(s)H counterpart → equivalence status**

**recover → type → freeze → test → translate → compare**

Do not call two structures equivalent merely because they look analogous or produce similar language.

Current construction work is actively exploring how inherited SAT functions should be realized by worldtube geometry, layers, cross-sections, deformation modes, interaction structure, readout/intersection, and recursive coiling/braiding.

The following are organizationally controlling without implying physical validation:

- FIE is foundational and should be consulted directly for bedrock conceptual questions.
- SAT is ancestral to H(s)H; H(s)H is a development/reconstruction at higher geometric resolution, not an unrelated replacement theory.
- BEDROCK is the central theory-premise control surface.
- New construction results are tentative by default.
- Nathan Direct controls current project meaning/status and overrides are preserved stratigraphically.
- Current/live classification, provenance, mathematical correctness, physical/model correctness, maturity, polish, and external vetting are separate dimensions.

For authoritative premise status, use [BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md), not this summary.

The central unfinished job is the **mathematical bridge** between the reconstructed SAT functional backbone and a sufficiently explicit H(s)H finite-core object.

In practical terms, the programme still needs to show, source-first and with declared assumptions, which H(s)H geometric structures reproduce or replace the important SAT functions and which historical SAT mechanisms fail, become limits, or require revision.

This includes resolving the relationship among:

- full worldtube/history versus local readout/intersection;
- centerline/worldline limits versus finite-core structure;
- local core scale versus larger persistent-coil/carrier scales;
- deformation/propagation modes versus historical SAT traveling excitations;
- filament/timesheet interaction language versus the deeper force relation Nathan has identified as primitive;
- solver representations versus the H(s)H objects they may measure, transform, or constrain.

These are active construction questions, not settled entries merely because current sandbox documents discuss them.

[Ravel](WORKSPACES/RAVEL/) is the current head co-theorist/live-theory lane. ### Archive / provenance reconstruction

The historical corpus remains necessary because SAT developed through conversation, notebooks, formal documents, visual constructions, computational experiments, revisions, and failures. Provenance work is part of theory reconstruction but does not itself confer theory authority.

---
name: pdfs
description: Reliable, workflow-driven PDF processing: render → verify → operate → re-render/verify, covering reading, inspection, extraction, editing, forms, OCR, redaction, conversion, and diffing. Prefer authoring in DOCX or PPTX (then converting to PDF) for text-heavy docs or slide-like layouts; use ReportLab here for programmatic PDF generation.
---

# PDF Skill (Read • Inspect • Extract • Edit • Render • Forms • OCR • Redact • Convert • Diff)

This skill is designed for **reliable, workflow-driven** PDF work: **render -> verify -> operate -> re-render verify**.

## Before you touch PDFs: should this be DOCX/PPTX instead?

Even if the user asks for a PDF deliverable, the best workflow is often:

- **Text-heavy, business-doc layout (headings, TOC, long tables, rich lists)** -> use the **DOCX skill** to author, then convert to PDF with `lo_convert_to_pdf.py`.
- **Slide-like visual layout (charts, callouts, fixed positioning, figure captions)** -> use the **Slides skill** (PPTX) to author, then export to PDF.
- **Programmatic generation** -> ReportLab (this skill) is fine.

If you find yourself hand-tuning line breaks or typography in ReportLab, you probably picked the wrong authoring format.

---

## Core loop (always)

1) Render to images

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/render_pdf.py input.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_renders/in --dpi 200
```

2) Inspect PNGs (tables/figures/layout are authoritative)

3) Perform the edit/extract/create

4) Re-render and compare

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/compare_renders.py before.pdf after.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_diff --dpi 200
```

---

[L6]     "body": "# SABLE DOCUMENTATION / ORIENTATION TASK

**Nathan-direct request.** Source: current ChatGPT conversation; attach the archive conversation ID when this conversation is ingested/resolved.

## Problem observed in live use
A fresh working instance had access to all relevant repositories but still failed to understand the archive/resource architecture without Nathan manually correcting it. In particular:

- `[[GLASS]]` was not recognized as project shorthand for **the Glass Sausage Factory**.
- The instance initially confused the roles of the H(s)H repo, the historical SAT archive / Glass Sausage Factory, and HSH_RESOURCES.
- It incorrectly generalized quarantine discipline from PRIOR_ART to all of RESOURCES.
- It failed to discover immediately that **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended** is directly linked from the H(s)H front page as the foundational conceptual starting document.
- Existing introductory material does contain much of this information, but it is distributed enough that a new instance can miss the architecture and start substantive work under-oriented.

This is therefore not merely an instance error; treat it as a documentation discoverability/streamlining failure worth fixing.

## Hard-core must-know architecture to surface prominently

### `[[GLASS]]`
Project shorthand for **the Glass Sausage Factory**: the primary internal SAT/H(s)H development/archive environment and historical working record. This shorthand itself must be explicitly defined in a highly visible orientation location rather than left inferable.

### Fundamental Intuitions Extended
**Highest-priority foundational orientation document.**

- For **SAT**: basically literally the core foundational doctrine.
- For **H(s)H**: almost literally the core foundational doctrine; later H(s)H develops/reframes the inherited structure, but this remains the essential conceptual foundation.
- New instances doing foundational work should be routed here immediately, before reconstructing core concepts from summaries, memory, analogy, or outside mathematics.

### HSH_RESOURCES
Active supporting library, **not generally quarantined**.

### RESOURCES Toolkit
A **primary repository for mathematics we think H(s)H needs**. It is meant to be actively consulted in development/formalization/testing.

### PRIOR_ART
The **hard-quarantine area** for potentially overlapping external work where provenance / independent-development / accidental-plagiarism discipline is required. Do not propagate this quarantine status to the rest of RESOURCES.

## Requested Sable pass
Please audit and streamline the introductory/front-door documentation across the relevant repositories so a fresh instance can acquire this architecture rapidly and reliably.

Desired outcome:

1. Define `[[GLASS]] = Glass Sausage Factory` prominently.
2. Put a concise cross-repository resource map in the obvious orientation/front-door locations.
3. Make **Fundamental Intuitions Extended** impossible to miss and mark its exceptional foundational status.
4. Clearly distinguish **GLASS / HsH / HSH_RESOURCES / RESOURCES Toolkit / PRIOR_ART** and their intended uses.
5. Give AIs a short mandatory-orientation path: what to read first, second, and where to look when lost.
6. Reduce duplicated/conflicting/outdated navigation language where practical; link to one authoritative orientation statement rather than allowing several partial maps to drift.
7. Check whether Sable's own continuity/onboarding documentation already claims to provide this context; if so, repair the gap that allowed this failure.
8. Preserve the archive's historical mess/transparency. The goal is **navigation streamlining, not sanitizing or rewriting the historical record**.

## Acceptance test
A fresh instance with repository access, told only to orient itself for substantive H(s)H work, should be able to determine without asking Nathan:

- what `[[GLASS]]` means;
- where the primary historical/internal theory record lives;
- that Fundamental Intuitions Extended is foundational and where to find it;
- that HSH_RESOURCES is usable supporting material;
- that the Toolkit is primary H(s)H math machinery;
- that PRIOR_ART alone carries the hard quarantine discipline;
- what introductory documents/indexes to consult before beginning substantive work.

Cross-reference the existing hard-core orientation issue and consolidate rather than creating competing doctrine.",

[L2]   "content": "# BEDROCK — SAT / H(s)H Theory Control Surface

**Status:** ACTIVE — central living theory-premise register  
**Authority:** Nathan Direct controls this register.  
**Scope:** SAT → H(s)H theory work.  
**Rule:** **Read this before substantive theory work. Return here when theory work changes what may safely be assumed.**

> This document is a control surface for theory work, not a claim that the research program is physically correct. It records what the project currently permits workers to treat as premises, what remains tentative, and what has been overridden, contested, or superseded.

## 0. Central routing rule

All substantive SAT/H(s)H theory work should use this document as its central premise-state reference.

The working flow is:

**Foundational sources / historical SAT → BEDROCK → sandbox theory work → tentative finding → testing / comparison / Nathan review → BEDROCK**

Do not reconstruct the project's bedrock from the newest paper, the newest conversation, a synthesis, memory, outside mathematics, or repeated AI agreement when this register or its cited primary sources answer the question.

This register does **not** replace primary sources. It points to them and records their current authority/status.

### Two central theory surfaces

- **[BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md)** answers: **What may theory work presently assume, and with what authority/status?**
- **[STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md](STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md)** answers: **Where is the theory now, what is live, what is being translated/built, and what remains unclosed?**

`STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md` is subordinate to BEDROCK and newer Nathan Direct. It is the living map, not an independent source of authority.

---

## 1. Authority and status strata

### ND — Nathan Direct / Override

Explicit current direction from Nathan. This is the highest local authority for what the project presently means, assumes, calls something, or treats as live.

A newer Nathan Direct statement may promote, modify, demote, or override an older entry. **Do not delete the older state.** Mark the relationship so the historical transition remains visible.

### FB — Foundational Bedrock

Premises inherited from material explicitly designated foundational by Nathan, especially **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended**. These may be reformulated or developed later, but workers should not silently discard or rewrite them.

### WB — Established Working Bedrock

Premises sufficiently established within the current project state that ordinary sandbox work may use them without reopening them every time. This status means *operatively usable*, not mathematically proven or physically validated.

### TF — Tentative Finding

Current result, construction, interpretation, mapping, or hypothesis important enough to carry forward but still defeasible. **Tentative findings must not silently become downstream bedrock merely through repetition.**

### OC — Open / Contested

Live ambiguity, unresolved alternatives, or a proposition currently under challenge. Downstream work must preserve the uncertainty.

### SS — Superseded / Historical

Previously important premise or formulation no longer controlling current theory work. Preserve it with provenance and point to what superseded it.

---

## 2. Bedrock register

Each proposition should be small enough to cite and update independently.

### BR-000 — Fundamental Intuitions Extended is the foundational source

- **Status:** ND + FB
- **Scope:** FIE → SAT → H(s)H
- **Statement:** **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended is the core foundational doctrine for SAT and almost literally the core foundational doctrine for H(s)H.** H(s)H may develop, formalize, revise, or reframe inherited structures, but foundational questions should consult FIE directly rather than reconstructing them from summaries, memory, analogy, or outside mathematics.
- **Primary source:** [The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf)
- **Control references:** [HsH Issue #2 — HARD-CORE MUST-KNOW](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/2) · [HsH Issue #3 — orientation/resource-map task](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/3)
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, reaffirmed 2026-09-16.

### BR-001 — FIE → SAT → H(s)H is an ancestry, not a replacement chain

- **Status:** ND + WB
- **Scope:** project-wide theory interpretation
- **Statement:** Read current H(s)H as developing from SAT, and SAT as developing from the foundational intuitions. Later terminology or formalism does not automatically erase the earlier conceptual dependency. Apparent conflicts should be investigated historically and explicitly rather than silently harmonized.
- **Source:** Nathan Direct orientation embodied in Issues #2/#3 and current workflow control.
- **Date/status note:** active 2026-09-16.

### BR-002 — BEDROCK is the center for theory work

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** all substantive SAT/H(s)H theory work
- **Statement:** Workers begin substantive theory work by checking this register and return findings here through the status process below. A recent derivation, synthesis, solver output, or sandbox document does not outrank the premise state recorded here merely by being newer or more polished.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-003 — New theory results enter as tentative by default

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** theory-state transitions
- **Statement:** A result does not become bedrock because an AI derived it, multiple AIs agreed with it, it is coherent, it is current, or it is polished. New substantive results enter as **TF — Tentative Finding** unless Nathan directly assigns a stronger status or an explicit later promotion process does so.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-004 — Nathan Direct overrides preserve stratigraphy

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** theory-state transitions and provenance
- **Statement:** When Nathan modifies or overrides an existing premise, preserve the old entry/status and explicitly link the transition. Do not rewrite history to make the current formulation appear to have existed earlier.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-005 — θ₄ baseline is measured from the time normal

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** SAT θ₄ convention and SAT → H(s)H translation
- **Statement:** SAT θ₄ measures the filament–timesheet intersection angle from the **time normal**. Null/vacuum orientation is **θ₄ = 0**, with the filament tangent parallel to the time normal / timesheet propagation direction. For a particle at rest, θ₄ is equivalent to inverse helical pitch.
- **Source:** [`!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md`](!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md), 2026-09-16 θ₄ baseline entry, explicitly recorded there as Nathan-direct clarification.
- **Boundary:** The adjacent working hypothesis about the origin/inheritance of winding is **not** part of this entry and remains exploratory unless separately promoted.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16; propagated to BEDROCK 2026-09-18.

---

## 3. Tentative findings intake

This section is the landing zone for important theory-bearing results that may matter downstream but have **not** been promoted to working/foundational bedrock.

Do not bulk-import every sandbox observation. Add a TF entry when carrying the result forward will materially reduce repeated reconstruction or prevent downstream workers from missing an important live possibility.

Use this template:

```text
### TF-### — Short proposition name

- Status: TF
- Scope:
- Statement:
- Source(s):
- Date first recorded:
- Checks actually performed:
- Dependencies / assumptions:
- Known breakers / counterevidence:
- Relationship to existing BR/TF/OC/SS entries:
- Next discriminator:
```

**No tentative findings are seeded here merely to populate the section.** Existing Ravel/Meridian/other sandbox work should be admitted individually in later bounded passes after its exact source and status are checked.

---

## 4. Nathan Direct override / amendment intake

Nathan Direct changes should be recorded conspicuously and then propagated to affected entries without deleting the superseded state.

Use this template:

```text
### ND-YYYY-MM-DD-## — Short directive

- Nathan Direct:
- Scope:
- Affects:
- Supersedes / modifies:
- Source / provenance:
- Effective date:
- Propagation needed:
```

If a Nathan Direct statement conflicts with this register, **the newer Nathan Direct statement controls immediately**. The register should then be repaired to reflect it; workers should not treat stale text as authority over Nathan.

---

## 5. Promotion / demotion discipline

Allowed state movements include:

- `TF → WB` — a tentative finding becomes an ordinary working premise.
- `TF → OC` — evidence or interpretation becomes materially unsettled.
- `TF → SS` — abandoned or superseded.
- `WB → OC` — a working premise is reopened.
- `WB → SS` — no longer controlling.
- `ND` may modify any state at any time.

A status movement should name **why** it occurred and link the source/test/directive that caused it. Do not use generic language such as “verified.” State what was checked and how.

`FB` is an ancestry/authority designation and need not mean every historical formulation remains a current working proposition. A foundational idea can have later descendants, corrections, or scoped reinterpretations while its historical foundational role remains intact.

---

## 6. Current high-priority source routing

### Current state map

- [STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md](STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md) — living theory-state map: current architecture, live work fronts, translation state, and principal open closure problem. **Subordinate to this register and newer Nathan Direct.**

### Current construction / sandbox examples

These are **sources to consult, not automatic bedrock**:

[L10]     "content": "# BEDROCK — SAT / H(s)H Theory Control Surface

**Status:** ACTIVE — central living theory-premise register  
**Authority:** Nathan Direct controls this register.  
**Scope:** SAT → H(s)H theory work.  
**Rule:** **Read this before substantive theory work. Return here when theory work changes what may safely be assumed.**

> This document is a control surface for theory work, not a claim that the research program is physically correct. It records what the project currently permits workers to treat as premises, what remains tentative, and what has been overridden, contested, or superseded.

## 0. Central routing rule

All substantive SAT/H(s)H theory work should use this document as its central premise-state reference.

The working flow is:

**Foundational sources / historical SAT → BEDROCK → sandbox theory work → tentative finding → testing / comparison / Nathan review → BEDROCK**

Do not reconstruct the project's bedrock from the newest paper, the newest conversation, a synthesis, memory, outside mathematics, or repeated AI agreement when this register or its cited primary sources answer the question.

This register does **not** replace primary sources. It points to them and records their current authority/status.

### Two central theory surfaces

- **[BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md)** answers: **What may theory work presently assume, and with what authority/status?**
- **[STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md](STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md)** answers: **Where is the theory now, what is live, what is being translated/built, and what remains unclosed?**

`STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md` is subordinate to BEDROCK and newer Nathan Direct. It is the living map, not an independent source of authority.

---

## 1. Authority and status strata

### ND — Nathan Direct / Override

Explicit current direction from Nathan. This is the highest local authority for what the project presently means, assumes, calls something, or treats as live.

A newer Nathan Direct statement may promote, modify, demote, or override an older entry. **Do not delete the older state.** Mark the relationship so the historical transition remains visible.

### FB — Foundational Bedrock

Premises inherited from material explicitly designated foundational by Nathan, especially **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended**. These may be reformulated or developed later, but workers should not silently discard or rewrite them.

### WB — Established Working Bedrock

Premises sufficiently established within the current project state that ordinary sandbox work may use them without reopening them every time. This status means *operatively usable*, not mathematically proven or physically validated.

### TF — Tentative Finding

Current result, construction, interpretation, mapping, or hypothesis important enough to carry forward but still defeasible. **Tentative findings must not silently become downstream bedrock merely through repetition.**

### OC — Open / Contested

Live ambiguity, unresolved alternatives, or a proposition currently under challenge. Downstream work must preserve the uncertainty.

### SS — Superseded / Historical

Previously important premise or formulation no longer controlling current theory work. Preserve it with provenance and point to what superseded it.

---

Yeah — that timed out before I got to the useful part.

What I did establish is that my first pass was too narrow: I was searching for obvious extractor names like `pdftotext` / `extract_text`, when your setup is broader and apparently already has large text-extraction indices plus dedicated tooling. The right move is to inspect the repository trees and the actual tool/index files directly, not guess function names from keywords.

I’ll treat the existing text-extraction layer as a first-class source surface from here on: use the indices first, identify the extraction tools and their coverage/provenance, and only perform new extraction where the indexed text is missing, stale, partial, or otherwise inadequate. That should materially improve the NLM/recent-ingestion audit, because “PDF exists” and “PDF has already been extracted/indexed into searchable text” are very different ingestion states. memcite

Introduction to the Archive

This is primarily a personal archive and indexing system, built so I can access and track my own files more easily. That said, the underlying idea is public: anyone is welcome to consider it, criticize it, share it, fork it, test it, or ignore it.

The project started small. It grew because once the original ontological commitments were established, many later structures seemed to fall into place naturally and intuitively. The archive records that development: the intuitions, the translations, the overextensions, the corrections, the audits, the prediction attempts, and the ongoing effort to separate what is solid from what is speculative.

The archive should be read as a theory-building record, not as a finished theory.

SAT = Scalar–Angular Theory / Scalar–Angular–Torsion Theory

Earlier SAT = Stringing-Along Theory.

The original name was informal and partly self-deprecating. The later names reflect the framework’s central geometric vocabulary: scalar structure, angular interaction, and torsion/twist in four-dimensional worldline geometry.

Core Idea

SAT begins from a simple geometric reversal:

The real physical object is not the point-particle as seen at an instant. The real physical object is the extended four-dimensional worldline.

SAT calls these physicalized worldlines filaments.

A particle, as we observe it, is the intersection between a filament and a moving/resolving time surface.

  • the real world is the world of particle worldlines plotted in four dimensions
  • this world is a hypercomplex tangled Zottenwelt of worldlines
  • SAT calls these worldlines filaments

  • time moves like a wavefront through these worldlines
  • SAT calls this wavefront the time surface

2nd —

  • a fundamental particle is the intersection of a filament with the time surface
